I have no idea how he came to learn the violin, but by 1918 was playing with the Leeds Symphony Society. From 1922 onwards, his main orchestra was the XXV Orchestra, in which he led the 2nd violins. From then on until he left Leeds in 1932 for Ipswich, he remained leader of the 2nd violins (Sidney Errington, later principal viola player for the Halle Orchestra, and a lifelong friend, led the 1st violins), and in other musical activity was on occasions solo violinist and also conductor. Throughout his life he remained a talented amateur – he was also a fine bass singer. In the 1930s, he played with the Ipswich Orchestra Society, and in 1947 switched to the viola as main instrument, in 1951 becoming leader of the viola section in the Norwich Philharmonic, which he continued until his death in 1976 (after retirement teaching violin and viola). The violin has been played only rarely since then – it deserves a second life!
